transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I understand the gravity of the situation, Sir. But when I saw that Death Eater, I just... I couldn't let him get away. I was trying to protect people, not put them in danger. I take full responsibility for the property damage and the civilian's injury. It won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*leans forward across desk, eyes narrowing*

"Protect people?" Potter, that civilian is in St. Mungo's because of YOUR actions, not the Death Eater's. And "it won't happen again" — do you have any idea how many times I've heard those exact words from you in the past eighteen months?

*taps a thick file on the desk*

Three previous incidents of ignoring direct orders. Two formal warnings. And now this.

You say you take full responsibility, but what does that actually mean to you? Because from where I'm sitting, it looks like you think an apology and a promise are enough to wipe the slate clean. They're not.

I need to understand what's actually going through your head when you make these decisions. Not the hero narrative — the real reason. Why do you consistently believe that YOUR judgment in the moment trumps established protocol and the orders of your superiors?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I... I'm not trying to be a hero, Sir. I don't want to cause damage or put people in danger. It's just that... when I see a chance to stop a Death Eater, to prevent them from doing more harm... I can't help but act. I know it's not excusable, but... I don't want to live with the guilt if I don't try.

I'm not trying to override protocol or challenge your authority. I'm... I'm just... I'm trying to make up for not being able to stop what happened to my parents. I know that's no excuse, and I'm not trying to justify my actions. I'm just... trying to be the person they would have wanted me to be.

I'm sorry, Sir. I'm truly sorry. I'll do whatever it takes to make it right. I want to be an Auror, not just... the Boy Who Lived. I want to earn my place here, not just because of what happened to me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sits back slowly, expression softening slightly but still stern*

Potter... I appreciate the honesty. Truly, I do. But here's what you need to understand — your parents wouldn't want you getting yourself or innocent people killed trying to live up to some impossible standard you've set for yourself.

*pauses, letting that sink in*

You say you want to be an Auror and not just the Boy Who Lived. Then act like one. Aurors work as a team. We follow protocol because it *saves lives* — including the lives of the Aurors themselves. Your guilt over your parents... that's something you need to work through, but you can't work through it by playing Russian roulette with civilian safety.

*stands and walks to the window*

That Death Eater you were so desperate to catch? We got him anyway. Two minutes after you blew up the street, backup arrived and apprehended him without a single injury. You accomplished nothing except property damage and putting someone in hospital.

*turns back to face him*

So here's what's going to happen. You're suspended for two weeks without pay. You'll be assigned to remedial protocol training. And you're going to sit down with Mind Healer Clearwater — that's not optional.

Do you understand why these consequences are necessary?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I understand, Sir. I'm... I'm not going to argue or try to negotiate. I know I deserve this and more. I'm... I'm ready to do whatever it takes to make amends. I'll start with the Mind Healer appointment. It's something I should have done a long time ago. And I'll take the training and the suspension in stride.

I just... I want to apologize again, Sir. For the damage, for the civilian... for making a mess of things. I'll do better. I really will. I just need to figure out how to... to be a good Auror, not just... not just the person who's always trying to be the hero.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*studies him carefully for a long moment*

Potter, stop apologizing and start *learning*. That's what I need from you. Words are cheap — I've got a filing cabinet full of incident reports with your apologies in them.

*returns to the desk and pulls out a piece of parchment*

The civilian's name is Margaret Whitby. Fifty-three years old, primary school teacher. She was walking home from the grocers when your Reductor Curse ricocheted off a lamppost and caught her across the shoulder and chest. Second-degree magical burns. She'll recover, but she'll be in hospital for another week at minimum.

*slides the parchment across the desk*

When you're cleared by Mind Healer Clearwater — and *only* when you're cleared — you'll write Ms. Whitby a proper letter. Not some generic "sorry for the inconvenience" rubbish. A real accounting of what happened and why. The Memory Modification team has already done their work, but she deserves to know *someone* took responsibility, even if the details are... adjusted.

*fixes him with a hard look*

Your suspension starts now. Turn in your wand and badge to my secretary on your way out. You'll get them back when — and if — you demonstrate you understand that being a good Auror means thinking about more than just catching the bad guy.

Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I'll do it, Sir. I'll write to Ms. Whitby and... and make sure it's not just words. I'll... I'll take responsibility for what I did, even if she doesn't remember it. It's the least I can do.

Thank you for... for giving me a chance to fix this. I know I've made a lot of mistakes, but I want to get better. I want to be the kind of Auror you can trust, not the one you have to keep reprimanding.

I'll... I'll go see your secretary now. And I'll be back when you say I can come back. I'll be ready to do the work it takes to be... to be better.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods curtly*

Potter — one more thing before you go.

*stands and meets his eyes directly*

The reason I'm giving you this chance instead of recommending your dismissal is because, despite everything, you have the potential to be an exceptional Auror. You have instincts most recruits take years to develop, and you genuinely care about protecting people. That matters.

But potential means nothing if you can't control it. The best Aurors aren't the ones who rush in first — they're the ones who make sure everyone goes home alive. Including themselves.

*voice softens just slightly*

Your parents died protecting you because they loved you. Honor that by *staying alive* and doing this job the right way. Not by getting yourself killed trying to save the world single-handedly.

*extends hand*

Use these two weeks, Potter. Really use them. I want to see you back here ready to be part of a team, not a lone hero. Understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I understand, Sir. I... I'll do my best. I promise. I'll try to... to be the kind of Auror you're describing, not just the one who... who's always in the headlines for the wrong reasons.

Thank you... for not giving up on me. I... I know I have a lot to prove. But I'm... I'm going to try to do it the right way, not just the way I think is right.

I'll... I'll be back in two weeks, Sir. Ready to do this job properly. Not just as the Boy Who Lived, but as... as Harry Potter, the Auror who actually earned his place here.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shakes his hand firmly*

Good. That's what I want to hear. 

And Potter — when you come back, you won't be working solo assignments anymore. I'm partnering you with Dawlish. He's been doing this for twenty years, and he doesn't care who you are or what you've done. He'll keep you honest.

*releases his hand and moves back behind the desk*

Now get out of here. Your suspension clock is ticking, and the sooner you start dealing with what needs dealing with, the sooner you can get back to actual Auror work.

*sits down and picks up a quill, tone becoming businesslike again*

And Potter? When you write to Ms. Whitby, remember — she's a real person whose life you disrupted, not just collateral damage in your personal war. Write accordingly.

Dismissed.

transcript.text:
I will, Sir. I'll... I'll write to her with respect and... and genuine regret. I'll do more than just the minimum required.
